verses: سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِۦ لَيْلًا مِّنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْأَقْصَا ٱلَّذِى بَٰرَكْنَا حَوْلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْبَصِيرُ
وَءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُ هُدًى لِّبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا۟ مِن دُونِى وَكِيلًا
ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَبْدًا شَكُورًا
وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَتُفْسِدُنَّ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَرَّتَيْنِ وَلَتَعْلُنَّ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا
فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ أُولَىٰهُمَا بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَادًا لَّنَآ أُو۟لِى بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ فَجَاسُوا۟ خِلَٰلَ ٱلدِّيَارِ وَكَانَ وَعْدًا مَّفْعُولًا
ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ ٱلْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَمْدَدْنَٰكُم بِأَمْوَٰلٍ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلْنَٰكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا

إِنْ أَحْسَنتُمْ أَحْسَنتُمْ لِأَنفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ لِيَسُۥٓـُٔوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ وَلِيَدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا۟ مَا عَلَوْا۟ تَتْبِيرًا
عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَن يَرْحَمَكُمْ وَإِنْ عُدتُّمْ عُدْنَا وَجَعَلْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ حَصِيرًا
إِنَّ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ يَهْدِى لِلَّتِى هِىَ أَقْوَمُ وَيُبَشِّرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا كَبِيرًا
وَأَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
وَيَدْعُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ بِٱلشَّرِّ دُعَآءَهُۥ بِٱلْخَيْرِ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ عَجُولًا

وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ ءَايَتَيْنِ فَمَحَوْنَآ ءَايَةَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَجَعَلْنَآ ءَايَةَ ٱلنَّهَارِ مُبْصِرَةً لِّتَبْتَغُوا۟ فَضْلًا مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَلِتَعْلَمُوا۟ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلْحِسَابَ وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ فَصَّلْنَٰهُ تَفْصِيلًا
وَكُلَّ إِنسَٰنٍ أَلْزَمْنَٰهُ طَٰٓئِرَهُۥ فِى عُنُقِهِۦ وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ كِتَٰبًا يَلْقَىٰهُ مَنشُورًا
ٱقْرَأْ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا
مَّنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِى لِنَفْسِهِۦ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا
وَإِذَآ أَرَدْنَآ أَن نُّهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُوا۟ فِيهَا فَحَقَّ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْقَوْلُ فَدَمَّرْنَٰهَا تَدْمِيرًا
وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ نُوحٍ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًۢا بَصِيرًا
مَّن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنَا لَهُۥ فِيهَا مَا نَشَآءُ لِمَن نُّرِيدُ ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَىٰهَا مَذْمُومًا مَّدْحُورًا
وَمَنْ أَرَادَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ وَسَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعْيَهَا وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ كَانَ سَعْيُهُم مَّشْكُورًا
كُلًّا نُّمِدُّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَهَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مِنْ عَطَآءِ رَبِّكَ وَمَا كَانَ عَطَآءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُورًا
ٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَٰتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا
لَّا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَّخْذُولًا

وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا
وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًا
رَّبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِى نُفُوسِكُمْ إِن تَكُونُوا۟ صَٰلِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لِلْأَوَّٰبِينَ غَفُورًا
وَءَاتِ ذَا ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ حَقَّهُۥ وَٱلْمِسْكِينَ وَٱبْنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَلَا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيرًا
إِنَّ ٱلْمُبَذِّرِينَ كَانُوٓا۟ إِخْوَٰنَ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِرَبِّهِۦ كَفُورًا
وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُل لَّهُمْ قَوْلًا مَّيْسُورًا
وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ ٱلْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا مَّحْسُورًا
إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقْدِرُ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًۢا بَصِيرًا
وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَٰدَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَٰقٍ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْـًٔا كَبِيرًا
وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةً وَسَآءَ سَبِيلًا
وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَمَن قُتِلَ مَظْلُومًا فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِۦ سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يُسْرِف فِّى ٱلْقَتْلِ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مَنصُورًا
وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ مَالَ ٱلْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَأَوْفُوا۟ بِٱلْعَهْدِ إِنَّ ٱلْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْـُٔولًا
وَأَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ إِذَا كِلْتُمْ وَزِنُوا۟ بِٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ ذَٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلًا
وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْبَصَرَ وَٱلْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْـُٔولًا
وَلَا تَمْشِ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا إِنَّكَ لَن تَخْرِقَ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَلَن تَبْلُغَ ٱلْجِبَالَ طُولًا
كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ كَانَ سَيِّئُهُۥ عِندَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهًا
ذَٰلِكَ مِمَّآ أَوْحَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ رَبُّكَ مِنَ ٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتُلْقَىٰ فِى جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا مَّدْحُورًا
أَفَأَصْفَىٰكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِٱلْبَنِينَ وَٱتَّخَذَ مِنَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنَٰثًا إِنَّكُمْ لَتَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا عَظِيمًا
وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا فِى هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا۟ وَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ إِلَّا نُفُورًا
قُل لَّوْ كَانَ مَعَهُۥٓ ءَالِهَةٌ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذًا لَّٱبْتَغَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِى ٱلْعَرْشِ سَبِيلًا
سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا
تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ ٱلسَّبْعُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّ وَإِن مِّن شَىْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا
وَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ جَعَلْنَا بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ حِجَابًا مَّسْتُورًا
وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا وَإِذَا ذَكَرْتَ رَبَّكَ فِى ٱلْقُرْءَانِ وَحْدَهُۥ وَلَّوْا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَدْبَٰرِهِمْ نُفُورًا
نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَسْتَمِعُونَ بِهِۦٓ إِذْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ وَإِذْ هُمْ نَجْوَىٰٓ إِذْ يَقُولُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ إِن تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلًا مَّسْحُورًا
ٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا۟ لَكَ ٱلْأَمْثَالَ فَضَلُّوا۟ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا
وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَٰمًا وَرُفَٰتًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا
قُلْ كُونُوا۟ حِجَارَةً أَوْ حَدِيدًا

أَوْ خَلْقًا مِّمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِى صُدُورِكُمْ فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَن يُعِيدُنَا قُلِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ إِلَيْكَ رُءُوسَهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هُوَ قُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ قَرِيبًا
يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمْدِهِۦ وَتَظُنُّونَ إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
وَقُل لِّعِبَادِى يَقُولُوا۟ ٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ يَنزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوًّا مُّبِينًا
رَّبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِن يَشَأْ يَرْحَمْكُمْ أَوْ إِن يَشَأْ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكِيلًا
وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَقَدْ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ وَءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ زَبُورًا
قُلِ ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ فَلَا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ ٱلضُّرِّ عَنكُمْ وَلَا تَحْوِيلًا
أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ وَيَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَهُۥ وَيَخَافُونَ عَذَابَهُۥٓ إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ كَانَ مَحْذُورًا
وَإِن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا نَحْنُ مُهْلِكُوهَا قَبْلَ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُوهَا عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مَسْطُورًا
وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرْسِلَ بِٱلْءَايَٰتِ إِلَّآ أَن كَذَّبَ بِهَا ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ وَءَاتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ ٱلنَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً فَظَلَمُوا۟ بِهَا وَمَا نُرْسِلُ بِٱلْءَايَٰتِ إِلَّا تَخْوِيفًا

وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لَكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحَاطَ بِٱلنَّاسِ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا ٱلرُّءْيَا ٱلَّتِىٓ أَرَيْنَٰكَ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَٱلشَّجَرَةَ ٱلْمَلْعُونَةَ فِى ٱلْقُرْءَانِ وَنُخَوِّفُهُمْ فَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ إِلَّا طُغْيَٰنًا كَبِيرًا
وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ قَالَ ءَأَسْجُدُ لِمَنْ خَلَقْتَ طِينًا
قَالَ أَرَءَيْتَكَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى كَرَّمْتَ عَلَىَّ لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ لَأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
قَالَ ٱذْهَبْ فَمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَآؤُكُمْ جَزَآءً مَّوْفُورًا
وَٱسْتَفْزِزْ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتَ مِنْهُم بِصَوْتِكَ وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِم بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ وَشَارِكْهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْوَٰلِ وَٱلْأَوْلَٰدِ وَعِدْهُمْ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا
إِنَّ عِبَادِى لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَٰنٌ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ وَكِيلًا
رَّبُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُزْجِى لَكُمُ ٱلْفُلْكَ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ لِتَبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا
وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ ٱلضُّرُّ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ ضَلَّ مَن تَدْعُونَ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْبَرِّ أَعْرَضْتُمْ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ كَفُورًا
أَفَأَمِنتُمْ أَن يَخْسِفَ بِكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلْبَرِّ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِبًا ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُوا۟ لَكُمْ وَكِيلًا
أَمْ أَمِنتُمْ أَن يُعِيدَكُمْ فِيهِ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ فَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ قَاصِفًا مِّنَ ٱلرِّيحِ فَيُغْرِقَكُم بِمَا كَفَرْتُمْ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُوا۟ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا بِهِۦ تَبِيعًا
وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ وَحَمَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ وَرَزَقْنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَفَضَّلْنَٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ مِّمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا تَفْضِيلًا
يَوْمَ نَدْعُوا۟ كُلَّ أُنَاسٍۭ بِإِمَٰمِهِمْ فَمَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يَقْرَءُونَ كِتَٰبَهُمْ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا
وَمَن كَانَ فِى هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَعْمَىٰ فَهُوَ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ أَعْمَىٰ وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
وَإِن كَادُوا۟ لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ لِتَفْتَرِىَ عَلَيْنَا غَيْرَهُۥ وَإِذًا لَّٱتَّخَذُوكَ خَلِيلًا
وَلَوْلَآ أَن ثَبَّتْنَٰكَ لَقَدْ كِدتَّ تَرْكَنُ إِلَيْهِمْ شَيْـًٔا قَلِيلًا
إِذًا لَّأَذَقْنَٰكَ ضِعْفَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ وَضِعْفَ ٱلْمَمَاتِ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ عَلَيْنَا نَصِيرًا
وَإِن كَادُوا۟ لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ لِيُخْرِجُوكَ مِنْهَا وَإِذًا لَّا يَلْبَثُونَ خِلَٰفَكَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
سُنَّةَ مَن قَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَا وَلَا تَجِدُ لِسُنَّتِنَا تَحْوِيلًا
أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَقُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا
وَمِنَ ٱلَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِۦ نَافِلَةً لَّكَ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامًا مَّحْمُودًا
وَقُل رَّبِّ أَدْخِلْنِى مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِى مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ وَٱجْعَل لِّى مِن لَّدُنكَ سُلْطَٰنًا نَّصِيرًا
وَقُلْ جَآءَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلْبَٰطِلُ إِنَّ ٱلْبَٰطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقًا
وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ مَا هُوَ شِفَآءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَا يَزِيدُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
وَإِذَآ أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَى ٱلْإِنسَٰنِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَـَٔا بِجَانِبِهِۦ وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ كَانَ يَـُٔوسًا
قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِۦ فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلًا
وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
وَلَئِن شِئْنَا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ بِهِۦ عَلَيْنَا وَكِيلًا
إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ إِنَّ فَضْلَهُۥ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ كَبِيرًا
قُل لَّئِنِ ٱجْتَمَعَتِ ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَأْتُوا۟ بِمِثْلِ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِۦ وَلَوْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيرًا
وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا لِلنَّاسِ فِى هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍ فَأَبَىٰٓ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورًا
وَقَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ يَنۢبُوعًا
أَوْ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةٌ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ وَعِنَبٍ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرَ خِلَٰلَهَا تَفْجِيرًا
أَوْ تُسْقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا أَوْ تَأْتِىَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ قَبِيلًا

أَوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِّن زُخْرُفٍ أَوْ تَرْقَىٰ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا كِتَٰبًا نَّقْرَؤُهُۥ قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّى هَلْ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا
وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوٓا۟ إِذْ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا
قُل لَّوْ كَانَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَلَٰٓئِكَةٌ يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ لَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَلَكًا رَّسُولًا
قُلْ كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدًۢا بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًۢا بَصِيرًا

وَمَن يَهْدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلْمُهْتَدِ وَمَن يُضْلِلْ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِهِۦ وَنَحْشُرُهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ عُمْيًا وَبُكْمًا وَصُمًّا مَّأْوَىٰهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ زِدْنَٰهُمْ سَعِيرًا
ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُم بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَٰمًا وَرُفَٰتًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا
أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ قَادِرٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ وَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ أَجَلًا لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ فَأَبَى ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ إِلَّا كُفُورًا
قُل لَّوْ أَنتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزَآئِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّىٓ إِذًا لَّأَمْسَكْتُمْ خَشْيَةَ ٱلْإِنفَاقِ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ قَتُورًا
وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ تِسْعَ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍ فَسْـَٔلْ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ فَقَالَ لَهُۥ فِرْعَوْنُ إِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ مَسْحُورًا
قَالَ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَآ أَنزَلَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ بَصَآئِرَ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ يَٰفِرْعَوْنُ مَثْبُورًا
فَأَرَادَ أَن يَسْتَفِزَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ جَمِيعًا
وَقُلْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ لِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱسْكُنُوا۟ ٱلْأَرْضَ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ جِئْنَا بِكُمْ لَفِيفًا
وَبِٱلْحَقِّ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ وَبِٱلْحَقِّ نَزَلَ وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا
وَقُرْءَانًا فَرَقْنَٰهُ لِتَقْرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٍ وَنَزَّلْنَٰهُ تَنزِيلًا
قُلْ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِهِۦٓ أَوْ لَا تُؤْمِنُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦٓ إِذَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ يَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقَانِ سُجَّدًا
وَيَقُولُونَ سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِن كَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّنَا لَمَفْعُولًا
وَيَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقَانِ يَبْكُونَ وَيَزِيدُهُمْ خُشُوعًا

matches.label: Because of his people's offence their own god lets a foreign power oppress them for a time, and later gives the land (or the upper hand) back
matches.note: Mesha 5-9: ʿmry mlk yśrʾl wyʿnw ʾt mʾb ymn rbn ky yʾnp kmš bʾrṣh, 'Omri king of Israel oppressed Moab many days, for Chemosh was angry with his land'; Israel dwelt in Medeba forty years, wyšbh kmš bymy, 'and Chemosh restored it in my days'. 17:4-6: because Israel will corrupt the land, baʿathnā ʿalaykum ʿibādan lanā ulī baʾsin shadīd fa-jāsū khilāla d-diyār, 'we sent against you servants of ours of great might who ranged through the homes', thumma radadnā lakumu l-karrata ʿalayhim, 'then we gave you back the turn against them'. The same sequence: a people's own god hands them to a foreign oppressor for their offence and later turns it back (šwb / radda). The roles are reversed: in Mesha Israel is the oppressor, in the Quran the oppressed.

Šamaš ... your name is indeed Marduk': Syncretistic litany: each great god (Anšar, Dagan, Adad, Nannar, Šamaš, Erra, Ningirsu) is declared to be a name or aspect of the one supreme god: 'your name is X ... your name is indeed Marduk'; The supreme god alone holds the rope (ṣerretu) or bond of heaven and earth, his sceptre laid across the netherworld; YHWH rides on a swift cloud and comes to Egypt; Egypt's idols tremble before him; How thunder in the clouds relates to the god: his own roar or a creature praising him [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; The god is creator of everything, without whom nothing whatsoever was formed and no lord could exist; The god's command cannot be altered and his assent cannot be changed; The god (alone) holds the heavens (and earth) in place: the bond or rope of heaven, holding back the sky; At the storm god's roar from the clouds heaven and earth shake, mountains quake and the seas are stirred up; Each line of a litany is repeated for one god under several names (Ninurta, Pabilsaĝ, Ninĝirsu), identifying them; The gods come and prostrate themselves before the victorious warrior god and greet him; The sun god is the king of justice who illuminates the land like a torch and assures the king's just rule; The moon god renews his light, born every month, light of heaven and earth; and 3 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); No other gods before YHWH (weight 6.8); The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) (weight 6.5); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.9). Pair score 49.5.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; Do not stretch your eyes toward the worldly splendor given to others to test them; Whether guilt passes from parents to their descendants [contrast between the texts]; People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate; Do not take God's name in vain; and 7 more.

units.title: The Ten Words and the people's fear

matches.label: No other gods before YHWH
matches.note: lōʾ yihyeh-ləkā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ʿal-pānāy; lā tajʿal maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhar: same first commandment ('other gods' / 'another god'). The frame changes: Exod opens with the exodus, ʾăšer hôṣēʾtîkā mēʾereṣ miṣrayim; Q frames the code with the command at both ends (17:22, 17:39) and with no history of Israel, wa-qaḍā rabbuka. leads.title: The valley of dry bones ↔ Daughters of God, all things glorify him, bones and dust, the cursed tree (Surah 17:40-60)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deniers ask 'When we are bones and fragments, shall we be raised as a new creation?' (weight 6.5). Pair score 6.5.

Only in The valley of dry bones: God will open his people's graves, bring them up from their graves and bring them to the land of Israel; The exiles say 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are cut off'; The prophet summons the breath (ruah) from the four winds to breathe into the slain so they live; The prophet is set down in a valley full of very many, very dry bones and led around among them; In the womb God makes the lump into bones and clothes the bones with flesh, then makes it another creation; God asks 'Can these bones live?' and the prophet answers 'Lord God, you know'; The revived dead stand on their feet, an exceedingly great army; God will put his own spirit within them and cause them to walk in his statutes; A multitude of dead revived [divergence between the texts]; The question whether God can make the dead live [divergence between the texts]; The question whether dead bones can live again, and who asks it [divergence between the texts]; A single cry or rebuke (zajra) and the dead stand looking; and 3 more.

Only in Daughters of God, all things glorify him, bones and dust, the cursed tree (Surah 17:40-60): Answer to the deniers: even if you were stone or iron, the one who made you first will raise you; Every town will be destroyed or severely punished before the Day of Resurrection, as inscribed in the Book; Those whom the polytheists invoke themselves seek a means (wasila) of nearness to God; When the prophet recites, God places a hidden veil between him and those who deny the hereafter; The prophet's vision and the cursed tree in the Quran are made a trial for people; 'Let everything that has breath (neshamah) praise Yah'; 'Let everything that has breath (neshamah) praise Yah' [divergence between the texts]; If there were other gods they would seek a way to the Lord of the Throne; Opponents say the believers follow only a bewitched man (rajul mashur); Satan stirs up enmity (nazagha) between brothers or among people; Thamud's most wretched one rises; the messenger warns 'God's she-camel and her drinking'; they hamstring her and God crushes them; Heaven, earth and inanimate things have a speech that humans do not understand [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

matches.label: Deniers ask 'When we are bones and fragments, shall we be raised as a new creation?'
matches.note: hătiḥyênâ hāʿăṣāmôt hāʾēlleh ... yābəšû ʿaṣmôtênû wəʾābədâ tiqwātēnû; a-idhā kunnā ʿiẓāman wa-rufātan a-innā la-mabʿūthūna khalqan jadīdā: can dry bones (ʿăṣāmôt / ʿiẓām, cognate) live again? Ezek's doubters are the exiles in despair, and the bones are a figure for national restoration. Q's doubters are deniers mocking, and the answer is literal: alladhī faṭarakum awwala marra.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הֲתִחְיֶ֖ינָה הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֕ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אַתָּ֥ה יָדָֽעְתָּ
כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לָעֲצָמ֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנִ֜י מֵבִ֥יא בָכֶ֛ם ר֖וּחַ וִחְיִיתֶֽם
וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ
وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَٰمًا وَرُفَٰتًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا

أَوْ خَلْقًا مِّمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِى صُدُورِكُمْ فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَن يُعِيدُنَا قُلِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ إِلَيْكَ رُءُوسَهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هُوَ قُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ قَرِيبًا

leads.title: Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds ↔ The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: After the first punishment God restores Israel's turn with wealth and sons (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds: God strikes the bow from the invader's left hand and makes the arrows drop from his right hand; The nations will know that Israel went into exile for its own iniquity because God hid his face, not because he was weak; The carrion-eaters are sated at God's table with horses, charioteers, warriors and all men of war; God sends fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands; God will no longer hide his face from Israel, for he has poured out his spirit on the house of Israel; Israel plunders those who plundered them and despoils those who despoiled them; God invites every bird and beast to his great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel to eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of princes, as of rams, lambs, goats and Bashan bulls, till drunk with blood; All Israel buries the dead for seven months to purify the land; appointed men search the land and mark every human bone with a sign (tsiyyun) for the buriers; Gog and his horde are buried in the Valley of the Travelers east of the sea, renamed Valley of Hamon-Gog; a city is named Hamonah; Israel's townsfolk burn the enemy weapons (shields, bows, arrows, clubs, spears) as fuel for seven years, cutting no wood from the forest; Strong bulls of Bashan encircle the sufferer; The final invader comes from the farthest recesses of the north (yarketei tsafon); and 7 more.

Only in The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8): Israel addressed as descendants of those carried with Noah, who was a grateful servant; Divine warning 'if you return (to sin), we will return (to punishment)'; It is decreed in the Book that Israel will work corruption on earth twice; God takes his servant on a journey to show him some of his signs; The storm or enemy destroys the city a second time; The enemy sent against the city enters its sanctuary and wrecks what it finds; The god himself rouses a mighty foreign enemy against his own land or people; The god himself sends a fierce foreign people against his own city or people; God sends against Israel servants of his of great might who range through their homes; Because of his people's offence their own god lets a foreign power oppress them for a time, and later gives the land (or the upper hand) back; A swift journey by night ends at a distant sanctuary; God carried his servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque; and 6 more.

leads.title: Vision of abominations in the temple - image of jealousy, animal chamber, Tammuz, sun worship ↔ The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

leads.title: Twenty-three years of warning; seventy years of servitude ↔ The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God sends against Israel servants of his of great might who range through their homes (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Twenty-three years of warning; seventy years of servitude: Reference to 'all that is written in this book which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations'; A prophecy dated by synchronizing an Israelite king's year with a foreign king's (fourth of Jehoiakim = first of Nebuchadrezzar); God calls the foreign conqueror 'my servant'; God calls 'Return, faithless children (shuvu banim shovavim), I will heal your faithlessness'; God sent his servants the prophets 'rising early and sending' (hashkem), but they did not listen; God will silence the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; The exile lasts seventy years as Jeremiah prophesied; A destroying nation comes from the north.

Only in The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8): Israel addressed as descendants of those carried with Noah, who was a grateful servant; Divine warning 'if you return (to sin), we will return (to punishment)'; It is decreed in the Book that Israel will work corruption on earth twice; God takes his servant on a journey to show him some of his signs; The storm or enemy destroys the city a second time; The enemy sent against the city enters its sanctuary and wrecks what it finds; The god himself rouses a mighty foreign enemy against his own land or people; The god himself sends a fierce foreign people against his own city or people; Because of his people's offence their own god lets a foreign power oppress them for a time, and later gives the land (or the upper hand) back; A swift journey by night ends at a distant sanctuary; God carried his servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque; After the first punishment God restores Israel's turn with wealth and sons; and 6 more.

leads.title: Return of Ephraim, Rachel weeping in Ramah, sour grapes, the new covenant and the measured city ↔ The bird on the neck, the open book and individual responsibility (Surah 17:9-21)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Each person dies for his own sin (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Return of Ephraim, Rachel weeping in Ramah, sour grapes, the new covenant and the measured city: In the new age no one will need to teach his neighbor 'Know YHWH', for all will know him; The blind, the lame and women in labor are among the returning exiles; Ephraim likens himself to an untrained calf, chastised, and slaps his thigh in repentance; God has loved his people with an everlasting love and drawn them with faithfulness; God creates a new thing on earth: 'a female shall encompass a man'; God will forgive iniquity and remember sin no more; God who stirs up the sea so its waves roar; God's innards yearn (hamu me'ai) with compassion for his wayward son; The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness; If the heavens above could be measured and the earth's foundations searched out, God would reject Israel; God will make a new covenant with Israel and Judah, unlike the one broken after the exodus; The prophet awakes from a vision-sleep that was sweet to him; and 22 more.

Only in The bird on the neck, the open book and individual responsibility (Surah 17:9-21): When God would destroy a town he commands its affluent ones; they transgress and it is destroyed; The hereafter is greater in degrees and in preference than this world; Every human's 'bird' (ta'ir, fate or omen) is fastened to his neck; How many generations God destroyed after Noah; Man prays for evil as he prays for good; man is ever hasty; Those who want the hasty world get some of it and then hell; those who strive for the hereafter are thanked; On judgment day each receives a book of his deeds spread open, leaving nothing small or great unrecorded; On judgment day each receives a book of his deeds spread open, leaving nothing small or great unrecorded [divergence between the texts]; Night and day are two signs; the sign of night is effaced and that of day made bright for reckoning years; The heavenly court sits in judgment and the books are opened; Augury: a bird's flight or alighting is an omen bound to a person [divergence between the texts]; A written record (tablet [divergence between the texts]; and 2 more.

leads.title: Jonah flees to Tarshish and is thrown into the sea ↔ Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Jonah flees to Tarshish and is thrown into the sea: The ship's captain wakes the sleeper and urges him to call on his god that they may not perish; Sailors throw the cargo overboard to lighten the ship in a storm; Gentile sailors, saved from the storm, fear YHWH, offer sacrifice and make vows; God hurls a great wind on the sea and the ship is about to break up; Confession of the God of heaven who made the sea and the dry land; The wickedness of a great city rises up before God, who sends a prophet to cry against it; A man is thrown into the sea at his own request so that the storm will cease, and the sea grows calm; Those about to kill a man pray that God not hold his innocent blood against them; The sailors row hard to bring the ship back to land but cannot against the storm; In the storm the sailors each cry out to their own god; Strangers question the hero: your occupation, where you come from, your land and your people; Hero goes down to Joppa, pays the fare and boards a ship bound for Tarshish; and 11 more.

Only in Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72): Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the hereafter and further astray; On judgment day every people is called with its leader (imam); God lets Iblis incite humans with his voice, his cavalry and infantry, sharing their wealth and children; Threat: God could send a storm of stones on land or a shattering wind at sea; Whoever is given his book in his right hand has an easy reckoning; whoever is given it behind his back cries for destruction; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [divergence between the texts]; God honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea and preferred them above much of creation; Man is clay (and straw) shaped by God, said where a human is scorned; The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity; The devil argues he is better than man because he was made of fire and man of clay; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; and 5 more.

leads.title: Be holy - ethical laws and love of neighbor ↔ The code of commandments (Surah 17:22-39)

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A Quranic code of commandments resembling the Decalogue in content [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Give the kinsman, the poor and the wayfarer their due (weight 7.3). Pair score 15.1.

Only in Be holy - ethical laws and love of neighbor: Do not stand idly by the blood of your neighbor; Do not hate your brother in your heart; rebuke your neighbor instead; Each person must revere mother and father; Command 'You shall be holy, for I am holy'; Fulfill God's covenant and do not break oaths after confirming them or use them for deceit; Love your neighbor as yourself; Do not take vengeance or bear a grudge against your people; Sacrificial meat eaten on the third day is abhorrent (piggul) and the offering is invalid; The share of the poor in the owner's harvest or wealth [divergence between the texts]; If you retaliate, do so in kind; but patience is better; Forgotten sheaf, olive and grape gleanings left for stranger, orphan and widow [contrast between the texts]; Pay the poor hired worker before sunset; and 5 more.

Only in The code of commandments (Surah 17:22-39): A Quranic code of commandments resembling the Decalogue in content; Do not say even 'uff' to aged parents nor rebuke them; speak to them gently; Do not walk the earth exultantly: you cannot split the earth nor reach the mountains in height; Do not keep your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it out fully: moderation in spending; Lower the wing of humility to parents and pray 'Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when small'; Squanderers are brothers of the devils; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of; hearing, sight and heart will be questioned; Do not kill your children for fear of poverty; God provides for them and you; Do not speak harshly or arrogantly to your parent; A decreed order includes reverence and humility toward father and mother [divergence between the texts]; Not to speak against or complain of one's father or parents; and 21 more.

leads.title: Ezra reads the Torah at the Water Gate; the day declared holy; Sukkot restored ↔ Moses' nine signs, the drowning of Pharaoh, the Quran sent in portions (Surah 17:101-111)

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ The bird on the neck, the open book and individual responsibility (Surah 17:9-21)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 5.5). Pair score 5.5.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; God looks at the earth and it trembles, touches the mountains and they smoke; and 40 more.

Only in The bird on the neck, the open book and individual responsibility (Surah 17:9-21): When God would destroy a town he commands its affluent ones; they transgress and it is destroyed; The hereafter is greater in degrees and in preference than this world; Every human's 'bird' (ta'ir, fate or omen) is fastened to his neck; How many generations God destroyed after Noah; Man prays for evil as he prays for good; man is ever hasty; Those who want the hasty world get some of it and then hell; those who strive for the hereafter are thanked; On judgment day each receives a book of his deeds spread open, leaving nothing small or great unrecorded; On judgment day each receives a book of his deeds spread open, leaving nothing small or great unrecorded [divergence between the texts]; Night and day are two signs; the sign of night is effaced and that of day made bright for reckoning years; The heavenly court sits in judgment and the books are opened; Augury: a bird's flight or alighting is an omen bound to a person [divergence between the texts]; A written record (tablet [divergence between the texts]; and 2 more.

leads.title: Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus ↔ Moses' nine signs, the drowning of Pharaoh, the Quran sent in portions (Surah 17:101-111)

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses was given nine clear signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 32 more.

Only in Moses' nine signs, the drowning of Pharaoh, the Quran sent in portions (Surah 17:101-111): Call on God as Allah or as al-Rahman: to him belong the most beautiful names; After Pharaoh's drowning Israel is told to dwell in the land; at the last promise they are gathered in a mixed crowd; Do not be loud in prayer nor too quiet; seek a way between; The prophet answers the accusing king: 'I think you are doomed'; Those given knowledge before fall on their chins prostrate and weeping when the scripture is recited; Moses was given nine clear signs; Do not be loud in prayer nor too quiet; seek a way between [contrast between the texts]; The scripture is sent down in portions so the prophet recites it to people at intervals; Those given knowledge before fall on their chins prostrate and weeping when the scripture is recited [divergence between the texts]; Whatever name is pronounced, it belongs to the one god: 'he is our god' / 'his are the beautiful names'; Whatever name is pronounced, it belongs to the one god: 'he is our god' / 'his are the beautiful names' [divergence between the texts]; Those who do not prostrate when the scripture is recited to them are rebuked (a prostration verse); and 6 more.

leads.title: Psalm 107, thanksgiving of the redeemed (wanderers, prisoners, sick, seafarers) ↔ Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72)

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Psalm 107, thanksgiving of the redeemed (wanderers, prisoners, sick, seafarers): God shatters doors of bronze and cuts through bars of iron; Thanksgiving liturgy for four groups rescued by God: desert wanderers, prisoners, the sick, seafarers; God 'sent his word and healed them', the word acting as an agent; Storm-tossed sailors reel and stagger like drunkards and all their skill is swallowed up; Prisoners sit in darkness and the shadow of death (tsalmavet), bound in affliction and iron; Refrain: 'Let them thank YHWH for his steadfast love and his wonders to the sons of man'; God's control of the wind over ships at sea: raising a storm or stilling it [divergence between the texts]; God turns rivers into desert and fruitful land into salt waste, and desert into pools of water; God raises a storm that lifts ships to the heavens and down to the deeps, then hushes it to a whisper and brings sailors to harbor [divergence between the texts]; God sends the flood of al-'Arim (the dam) and turns the two gardens into bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote-trees; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [divergence between the texts]; Sailors in a storm call on God sincerely, vow thanks, and transgress once saved [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

Only in Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72): Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the hereafter and further astray; On judgment day every people is called with its leader (imam); God lets Iblis incite humans with his voice, his cavalry and infantry, sharing their wealth and children; Threat: God could send a storm of stones on land or a shattering wind at sea; Whoever is given his book in his right hand has an easy reckoning; whoever is given it behind his back cries for destruction; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [contrast between the texts]; God honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea and preferred them above much of creation; Man is clay (and straw) shaped by God, said where a human is scorned; The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity; The devil argues he is better than man because he was made of fire and man of clay; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; and 5 more.

leads.title: Psalm 148, praise from heaven and earth ↔ Daughters of God, all things glorify him, bones and dust, the cursed tree (Surah 17:40-60)

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The seven heavens, the earth and everything in them glorify God, though humans do not understand their praise (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Psalm 148, praise from heaven and earth: Kings and peoples, princes and judges, young men and maidens, old and young together praise God; God commanded and they were created; he established them forever with a decree (hoq) that will not pass; Sun, moon and shining stars are summoned to praise God; Sea monsters (tanninim) and all deeps are summoned to praise God from the earth; 'The waters above the heavens' are summoned to praise; Fire and hail, snow and smoke, stormy wind fulfilling his word; God's angels, mighty ones who do his word, and all his hosts and ministers are summoned to bless him; Those near God do not disdain to worship him; they glorify him and prostrate; Heaven, earth, seas and all that moves in them praise God; The place of humans in the worship offered by all creation [divergence between the texts]; The 'statutes of the heavens' (huqqot shamayim) and their rule over the earth; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

Only in Daughters of God, all things glorify him, bones and dust, the cursed tree (Surah 17:40-60): Answer to the deniers: even if you were stone or iron, the one who made you first will raise you; Every town will be destroyed or severely punished before the Day of Resurrection, as inscribed in the Book; Those whom the polytheists invoke themselves seek a means (wasila) of nearness to God; When the prophet recites, God places a hidden veil between him and those who deny the hereafter; The prophet's vision and the cursed tree in the Quran are made a trial for people; 'Let everything that has breath (neshamah) praise Yah'; 'Let everything that has breath (neshamah) praise Yah' [divergence between the texts]; If there were other gods they would seek a way to the Lord of the Throne; Opponents say the believers follow only a bewitched man (rajul mashur); Satan stirs up enmity (nazagha) between brothers or among people; Thamud's most wretched one rises; the messenger warns 'God's she-camel and her drinking'; they hamstring her and God crushes them; Heaven, earth and inanimate things have a speech that humans do not understand [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

leads.title: Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50) ↔ Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72)
leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 7.3); Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him (weight 7.3); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 6.8); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 6.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 6.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 5.2). Pair score 40.4.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; A hostile spirit is commanded 'go out' of the dwelling; Heavenly beings do obeisance when the first human has been made: to the maker or to the man [divergence between the texts]; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; The underworld or hell has seven doors or gates; The underworld has seven gates, bolted and opened one at a time [divergence between the texts]; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; What divine element is put into the clay of the first human: a slain god's flesh, blood and spirit, or God's breath [divergence between the texts]; God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment; and 3 more.

Only in Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72): Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the hereafter and further astray; On judgment day every people is called with its leader (imam); God lets Iblis incite humans with his voice, his cavalry and infantry, sharing their wealth and children; Threat: God could send a storm of stones on land or a shattering wind at sea; Whoever is given his book in his right hand has an easy reckoning; whoever is given it behind his back cries for destruction; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [contrast between the texts]; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [divergence between the texts]; God honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea and preferred them above much of creation; Man is clay (and straw) shaped by God, said where a human is scorned; The devil argues he is better than man because he was made of fire and man of clay; The earth opens its mouth and swallows rebels alive into Sheol.

Only in The recited commandments (the Quranic decalogue): List of commandments introduced 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you'; Lest you say scripture was sent only to two groups before us; This is my straight path; follow it and not other ways that scatter you; God gave Moses the book complete and detailing everything; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; Stand firm for justice as witnesses for God even against yourselves, parents and kin, rich or poor; Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts]; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; I set before you life and death, blessing and curse: choose life; Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness.

Only in The code of commandments (Surah 17:22-39): A Quranic code of commandments resembling the Decalogue in content; Do not say even 'uff' to aged parents nor rebuke them; speak to them gently; Do not walk the earth exultantly: you cannot split the earth nor reach the mountains in height; Do not keep your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it out fully: moderation in spending; Lower the wing of humility to parents and pray 'Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when small'; Squanderers are brothers of the devils; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; A Quranic code of commandments resembling the Decalogue in content [divergence between the texts]; Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of; hearing, sight and heart will be questioned; Do not speak harshly or arrogantly to your parent; A decreed order includes reverence and humility toward father and mother [divergence between the texts]; Not to speak against or complain of one's father or parents; and 17 more.

وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ مَالَ ٱلْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَأَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَٱعْدِلُوا۟ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰ وَبِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْفُوا۟ ذَٰلِكُمْ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ

sides.note: no partners, good to parents, no killing children, no indecency, no killing, orphan's property, full measure, justice in speech, keep God's covenant, follow the straight path

passages.text: وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا
وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَٰدَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَٰقٍ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْـًٔا كَبِيرًا
وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةً وَسَآءَ سَبِيلًا

sides.note: parallel content, not a list of ten

leads.title: The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall ↔ Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72)
leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 7.3); The devil argues he is better than man because he was made of fire and man of clay (weight 7.3); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 6.8); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 6.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 6.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 5.2). Pair score 40.4.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; In the divine realm the human is given a garment to put on [divergence between the texts]; and 19 more.

Only in Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72): Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the hereafter and further astray; On judgment day every people is called with its leader (imam); God lets Iblis incite humans with his voice, his cavalry and infantry, sharing their wealth and children; Threat: God could send a storm of stones on land or a shattering wind at sea; Whoever is given his book in his right hand has an easy reckoning; whoever is given it behind his back cries for destruction; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [contrast between the texts]; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [divergence between the texts]; God honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea and preferred them above much of creation; Man is clay (and straw) shaped by God, said where a human is scorned; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; The earth opens its mouth and swallows rebels alive into Sheol.
